findings.title: Conditional include hook never runs due to missing `?`
findings.body: File app/serializers/user_serializer.rb defines `def include_website_name` without a question mark. Every other conditional in the same serializer is named `include_<attr>?` (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_stats?`, `include_user_fields?`), which is the convention ActiveModel::Serializer looks for. Because the name does not match, the hook is never called and `website_name` is always serialized, even when `website` is blank (as nil), adding noise to the payload and defeating the intended `website.present?` guard.

findings.title: `website_name` leaks for TL0 users seen as anonymous
findings.body: File app/serializers/user_serializer.rb adds `:website_name` to the serialized `attributes` list but does not add it to the `untrusted_attributes` list (`bio_raw`, `website`, `location`, etc.). The custom `include_website_name` guard only checks `website.present?` and does not check `scope.restrict_user_fields?`. Therefore an anonymous viewer of a TL0 user will have `website` suppressed but will still receive `website_name` (derived directly from the hidden website), leaking the private host/path the restriction was meant to hide. The spec's `untrusted_attributes` array has the same omission.

findings.title: Repeated unrescued URI parsing can raise and drops port/query
findings.body: File app/serializers/user_serializer.rb in `website_name` rescues `URI(website.to_s).host` with `rescue nil` but then calls `URI(website.to_s).path` two more times without rescue. A malformed `website` value that returns nil host on the first parse will raise `URI::InvalidURIError` on the later parses, turning a profile render into a 500. Even for valid URLs the display is lossy: only `host + path` is kept, so port (`example.com:8080`), query string, and fragment are silently dropped, and a site-relative or scheme-less value yields nil host so the link disappears in the template even though `model.website` exists.
